reviews.head: Plump Helmet Roast, Fourth Table from the Well
reviews.body: The plump helmet arrived plump, which I respect. The roast arrived roasted, which I also respect. The chair did not arrive, because a hauler took it mid-meal to a stockpile. I finished standing, like an animal, or an elf.

reviews.head: The Dining Hall, Recently Engraved
reviews.body: Eating beneath a masterful engraving of a dwarf being struck by a carp changes a meal. The stew was fine. I could not stop looking at the carp. The carp looked back. Portions generous; ambience aquatic and threatening.

reviews.head: The Lavish Biscuit Platter
reviews.body: Seven ingredients, one biscuit. The cook called it lavish, then threw a mug at me for asking what was in it. I can now confirm at least one ingredient was the mug. Crunchy. Memorable. Bruising.

reviews.head: Raw Turtle, Served Unshelled
reviews.body: The kitchen insists raw turtle is a delicacy. I insist it is a turtle. We agreed to disagree while the turtle quietly left the table. Service was slow; the entree was slower. One star for effort, one for cardio.

reviews.head: 'The Overseer Who Forgot Beds,' a Tragedy in Three Acts
reviews.body: The cast, hastily reassigned from hauling, delivered every line while carrying a stone. Act Two was lost when the lead wandered off for a drink. Act Three was a tantrum, possibly improvised. Moving. Literally: the stage was moved twice.

reviews.head: 'The Dance of the Dug Too Deep'
reviews.body: The troupe's interpretation of a forgotten beast rising from the third cavern was so convincing that the militia captain charged the lead dancer. A triumph of physical theatre. The encore was declined on the advice of the hospital.

reviews.head: 'Kobold Thief,' a One-Dwarf Show
reviews.body: The performer crept across the stage, took a goblet from the front row, and left. We assumed it was part of the show. It was not part of the show. The goblet remains missing. Bold staging. I would return if I owned more goblets.

reviews.head: 'Raised Again!' The Undead Musical
reviews.body: A traveling troupe of former corpses dance tirelessly, because they cannot tire. The choreography is relentless and slightly grabby. Act Two ended early when the militia arrived. Afterward, nobody could tell the cast from the audience. Haunting.

reviews.head: 'Ode to Granite,' Recited at {fort}
reviews.body: Forty stanzas about granite. To be fair, each was about a different block. The bard's command of grey is unmatched. By stanza thirty, three listeners had achieved the stillness of granite themselves. Recommended for masons and the very patient.

reviews.head: 'The Sky Is Too Big,' a Lament
reviews.body: A raw piece from a former surface hauler. The line 'it goes up and it does not stop' drew audible sobbing. Several listeners fled to the deepest bedroom available. Accurate, harrowing, and best enjoyed under at least forty feet of rock.

reviews.head: Limericks of the Militia
reviews.body: Every limerick ended on the word 'axe,' including the ones about weather and the one about a lovely aunt. Rhyme scheme: aggressive. Meter: marching. The commander recited from inside the danger room, so several lines were interrupted by spears.

reviews.head: 'Socks,' an Epic in Free Verse
reviews.body: The poet wept describing a single lost sock, then wept harder when another sock turned up, unrelated. Free verse suits the subject; socks also refuse to stay in pairs. Long. Damp. Universal. Every dwarf has lost a sock, and this poem knows it.

reviews.head: 'On the Nature of Rocks'
reviews.body: The library's newest acquisition argues, across three hundred pages, that rocks exist. The evidence is persuasive, mainly because the book itself is carved on a slab. A bold thesis. A sequel, 'Rocks, Further,' is reportedly underway during a strange mood.

reviews.head: 'The Bookkeeper's Ledger, Unabridged'
reviews.body: At last, a full inventory of every stockpile, read aloud by its author. The twist on page forty, where three barrels turn out to be one barrel counted three times, left the room gasping. Gripping for a list. Accuracy: low, as tradition demands.

reviews.head: 'Elves: A Field Guide'
reviews.body: Chapter one: they like trees. Chapter two: they like trees more than you. Chapter three is a single loving illustration of a tree, which I suspect was slipped in by an elf at the bindery. Informative, if leafy.

reviews.head: 'A History of {world}, Volume Nine'
reviews.body: Volumes one through eight were eaten by a forgotten beast, which the author treats as a review. Volume nine covers only Tuesdays. It is extremely thorough on Tuesdays. Readers seeking other days should consult the necromancer, who attended most of them.

reviews.head: 'Fear of the Sky: A Self-Help Guide'
reviews.body: The author recommends staying indoors, looking up only in emergencies, and never trusting a cloud. Includes a helpful diagram labelled 'up.' I read it underground, by lamplight, and felt deeply seen. Practical advice for practical dwarves.

reviews.head: The Tavern Band's Spring Residency
reviews.body: Drum, flute, and a dwarf who plays the table. The table was the standout. Their closer, 'Why Is There a Moat,' had the tavern stamping. A cat joined the chorus. Then thirty cats joined. Seating was limited by cats.

reviews.head: Solo Lyre Recital, the Well Room
reviews.body: The acoustics near the well are superb, as is the risk of falling in, which the lyrist did mid-ballad. The final note, echoing up from the bottom of the well, was the evening's high point. Haunting. She is fine. Damp, but fine.

reviews.head: 'Song of the Hammerer'
reviews.body: A work chant performed by the hammerer himself, with percussion supplied by the dwarf being sentenced. Rhythmically flawless, ethically debatable. Local justice has never sounded tighter. Bring earplugs and, ideally, a spotless record.

reviews.head: The Hospital Choir
reviews.body: Twelve patients, twelve splints, one dream. Their rendition of 'Bring Me Water, Nobody Is Bringing Me Water' captures the soul of dwarven medicine. The applause was thunderous. Nobody brought them water.

reviews.head: 'Where Do We Sleep?' A Migrant Opera
reviews.body: It opens with seven new arrivals singing 'Where do we sleep?' and closes with the overseer singing 'The hall, for now.' Tender and true, and staged entirely in a corridor, because the beds are still in the carpenter's queue.

reviews.head: The New Pump Stack
reviews.body: Seven screw pumps rise in a tower of pure ambition, moving water from where water was to where dwarves now are. The engineer calls it elegant. The dwarves at the bottom said something too, mostly in bubbles. Striking design.

reviews.head: The Trade Depot Annex
reviews.body: Wide enough for wagons, provided the wagons are small, the merchants patient, and the trees cut. The trees were not cut. The caravan turned back. A beautiful building in which nothing has ever been traded.

reviews.head: The Overseer's Office
reviews.body: Smoothed walls, engraved floors, and a door that locks from the inside. Visitors report it also locks from the outside. Masterful use of space, provided the space you want is the inside of a room you cannot leave.

reviews.head: The Great {stone} Hall
reviews.body: Built entirely of {stone}, which the masons pointed out repeatedly while I tried to eat. The pillars are generous. The tables are generous. The echo is so generous it repeats your complaints back to you, louder and in better grammar.

reviews.head: The Grand Danger Room
reviews.body: Upright spears in a gleaming grid. Recruits emerge tougher; visitors emerge shorter. The architect insists it is for training only. I was not training. I was looking for the privy. Bold, functional, and badly signposted.

reviews.head: Coffin Row
reviews.body: A long, solemn hall of slabs and coffins, lovingly engraved. Every ghost in the fort has stopped by to compliment it, which is precisely the problem. Silent, dignified, and occasionally screaming. A triumph of afterlife hospitality.

reviews.head: This Season's Sock Trend
reviews.body: Socks are back. They never left, but everyone lost one, so this season they are back in pairs. Mismatched pairs are now formal wear. Matched pairs are considered suspicious. No one has seen a complete set since the founding.

reviews.head: Rags Couture
reviews.body: The look among veteran miners: clothing worn until it is technically a rumor. Tattered tunics, boots held together by grudges, and the haunted stare of a dwarf who will not visit the clothier. Raw. Daring. Bad for morale.

reviews.head: {masterwright}'s Latest Helm
reviews.body: A helm so finely made the wearer forgets fear, gravity, and their own name. Menacing spikes, a gentle sheen, and an image of the wearer's grandmother being struck by a crossbow bolt. Chic. Protective. Strangely emotional.

reviews.head: Elven Caravan Couture
reviews.body: The visitors wore gowns of woven leaves and refused to trade for anything made of wood. Admittedly radiant. Unfortunately, a goat ate one of the outfits while the elf was still wearing it. Diplomatically disastrous, aesthetically bold.

reviews.head: The Tavern on Level Minus Twelve
reviews.body: Damp walls, warm ale, and a keeper who knows your name and your preferred mug to throw. Fights break out on a reliable schedule. The bard is decent. The beer shortage is not. Will return the moment there is beer.

reviews.head: The Upside-Down Mug
reviews.body: Built beside the magma forge, which keeps the beer warm and the patrons warmer. Wonderful atmosphere, in that the air visibly glows. I lost my eyebrows but kept my seat. Recommended for dwarves with spare eyebrows.

reviews.head: The Dry Barrel
reviews.body: Supplies are so low the tavern now serves 'the memory of wine.' Patrons hold empty mugs and sigh. The keeper pours nothing with great ceremony. Tantrum count: rising. Atmosphere: haunted by sobriety. Brewers, please hurry.

reviews.head: The Cozy Burrow
reviews.body: Barrels stacked to the ceiling, then stacked on the ceiling, which seems structurally optimistic. Every drink you could want and several you should not. I tried the rum and heard colors. Five stars, awarded shortly before I slept under the table.

reviews.head: The Kitchen of the Strange Mood
reviews.body: Not a restaurant: a cook in a fey mood seized the kitchen, demanding shells. We waited. Three days later she produced a single biscuit adorned with bone and declared it finished. Nobody may eat it. Best meal I never had.

reviews.head: Vegetable Night (Again)
reviews.body: The kitchen apologizes for the lack of meat with plump helmets in four forms: whole, sliced, mashed, and 'surprise,' which was also a plump helmet. The surprise is that it worked. Hearty, earthy, and confidently helmet-forward.

voxpops.q: What do you think of the new dining hall?
answers: The tables are lovely. I'd know, I hauled them all. Twice.
As a mason, I only see the joints. The joints are acceptable.
Is it new? I've been sleeping in here since I arrived.
I require a private dining room. This is a mandate, technically.
Good place to eat. Better place to throw a mug.
A cat ate my biscuit and then took my seat. Five stars.

voxpops.q: How do you feel about the sky?
answers: I don't. I won't. Next question.
I hauled a log on the surface once. I still see it when I close my eyes.
Fine as long as it stays up there. I check daily.
I'm a hunter. I've gotten used to it. I hate that I've gotten used to it.
The sky owes me a sock. The wind took it.
My grandmother says it's just a very tall ceiling. She's lying.

voxpops.q: What's your favorite drink and why?
answers: Wine. Because the beer was gone.
Ale. The only thing I've brewed that didn't explode.
Whatever's nearest the forge. It's always warm.
Water. I'm in the hospital. Not by choice. Nobody brings it.
Rum. We have plenty. Or none. I'm the bookkeeper, it's one of those.
I'm a child. I've been told to say milk. Milk.

voxpops.q: Have you seen the missing sock?
answers: Which one? There are dozens. We are a fort of the one-socked.
Yes. It's in a stockpile. I put it there. I'm a hauler. I regret nothing.
I saw a kobold wearing it as a hat. Looked good on him, honestly.
I'm the clothier and I'm not answering that.
My cat brought me one this morning. It was not my sock.
I wear it on my hand now. It's a puppet. His name is Urist.

voxpops.q: What would you do as overseer for a day?
answers: Beds. For everyone. Imagine it.
Ban the word 'haul' and see what happens.
Unpause. Just once. See how it goes.
Order a statue of myself. Then another, facing the first one.
Wall off the river. I've got reasons. They have fins.
Put the militia on dining duty. Nobody would dare complain.

voxpops.q: Should the fort get more cats?
answers: We don't 'get' cats. Cats get us.
Yes. I'm a cat. I'm kidding. Or am I. I'm a miner.
No. My workshop is now a cat workshop.
As the butcher, I abstain, loudly.
They keep the rats down, and the mood up, and my bed full.
Ask the cats. They'll tell you. Constantly. At four in the morning.

voxpops.q: What's the best thing you've ever crafted?
answers: A mug with a picture of a mug on it. Very meta. Very ☼.
A door. It opens. It closes. People don't appreciate that enough.
A crown, during a strange mood. I don't remember it. I'm told it's nice.
A splint. Nobody wants to see it, which is how you know it worked.
A cage, for the elf who said my carving was 'charming.'
Friendships. Also a granite throne. Mostly the throne.

voxpops.q: How do you prepare for a goblin siege?
answers: I pull the lever. Every lever. I don't know what they do.
Sharpen my axe, say goodbye to my cat, march out.
Stock the tavern. If we go, we go hydrated.
Lock myself in the archive. Goblins can't read.
Carry my baby to the front lines. Everyone else is doing it.
Pray to the trap designer. He's the real hero.

voxpops.q: What's the strangest thing in your bedroom?
answers: A boulder. I didn't put it there. Nobody admits to it.
A second bed. I'm not married. I'm just ready.
Twelve cats and a stranger. The stranger has also adopted the cats.
An engraving of me sleeping. Done while I slept.
A crack in the wall that hums at night.
Nothing. It's a hallway. I live in a hallway.

voxpops.q: What are you thankful for this {season}?
answers: Stone. There's so much of it. I'm a mason, it's a good year.
My friends, my family, and that the carp stayed in the river.
Booze. Sorry. I mean the gift of the brewers.
That I wasn't drafted. Yet. Please don't read this out.
My new boots. Both of them.
The ceiling. Specifically that it's still where it was.

voxpops.q: Thoughts on the elves who just visited?
answers: They hugged a tree in the depot. The depot is stone.
They wouldn't buy my wooden bowl. It's a beautiful bowl.
One of them called my beard 'rustic.' I'm still angry.
They were polite. Suspiciously polite.
I'm a woodcutter. I hid. It felt right.
They left. That was my favorite part.

voxpops.q: What would you name our next fortress?
answers: Somewhere Dry.
Not By The River.
Beerhold. Simple. Honest.
Fort Fort. You'd never forget it.
Whatever the noble wants, said loudly, so he hears me.
I'd name it after my cat. The cat would accept nothing less.

voxpops.q: Have you ever been in a strange mood?
answers: Once. I came out of it holding a sword. I'm a cheesemaker.
No, but I've been in a bad one. Does that count?
I don't remember. People keep thanking me for a necklace.
I tried. Asked for shells. They gave me a bucket of shells. Mood left.
Yes. I made a bed out of bone. It's comfortable. Nobody visits.
My spouse is in one now. I'm just leaving food at the door.

voxpops.q: How do you feel about {promoted} as {post}?
answers: They'll be fine. Probably. Pass the wine.
They took my office. I mean, they're very qualified.
Good for them. Can they get us beds?
Their first mandate was crowns. Their second was more crowns.
I knew them when they were just hauling dung. Now look.
I voted for the cat. Nobody listens to me.

voxpops.q: What do you think is in the cavern below?
answers: Mushrooms, big ones. I'd know, I'm a herbalist.
Something with fifty eyes. Possibly fifty somethings with one eye.
My old pick. I dropped it there. I'm not going to get it.
A whole troglodyte society that thinks we're the cavern.
The answer to all our problems. Or the cause of them.
I'm a child and I'm not allowed to talk about the cavern.

voxpops.q: How do you spend your break?
answers: Tavern, then nap, then tavern.
I watch the well. It's soothing until it isn't.
I read 'On the Nature of Rocks.' I'm on page four.
Sparring. I'm militia. My break is also my job. I'm tired.
I talk to the goats. They don't haul either.
Break? I'm a hauler. What is a break?

voxpops.q: What's the best room in {fort}?
answers: The tavern. Next question.
The library. Quiet, warm, and nobles never go there.
My workshop. It's mine. I've got a sign.
The dining hall, before the cats get there.
The hospital, if you like the ceiling.
The trade depot, when the caravan has cheese.

voxpops.q: What should we do with all this stone?
answers: Mugs! Hundreds of mugs! Endless mugs!
Blocks. Then walls. Then more walls.
Throw it at the goblins. Have we tried that?
I'm sleeping on a pile of it. It's fine. It's actually fine.
Give it to the elves. As a joke.
More statues of me, please. I'm the mayor.

voxpops.q: What's your earliest memory?
answers: Being carried into a goblin fight. Mum had a shield. I had a rattle.
A carp. Just a carp. I don't want to talk about it.
The smell of plump helmets roasting. Home.
The wagon ride here. Nobody would stop to let me pee.
Our old fort flooding. Forty dwarves holding their breath.
Mining. I was born holding a pick. Mum's still sore about it.

voxpops.q: Do you believe in ghosts?
answers: I believe in ghosts like I believe in cats. There are too many.
One rearranged my workshop. The new layout is better, actually.
Not until last night. Now very much yes.
I'm a priest. I believe in everything. It's in the contract.
The ghost of my uncle still owes me 5☼. I'm haunting HIM.
I'm a ghost. You're asking a ghost. Yes.

voxpops.q: What advice would you give new migrants?
answers: Don't sleep in the hall long. That's how it gets permanent.
Learn the levers. Don't touch the levers. Know the levers.
Make friends with the brewer. Trust me.
Socks. Bring extra socks.
Don't look up. Ever. You'll understand on your first harvest.
Avoid eye contact with the noble. It counts as volunteering.

voxpops.q: What's the worst job you've been assigned?
answers: Refuse pile duty. I'll be fine. I'll be fine eventually.
Clearing the moat. With my hands.
Feeding the forgotten beast in the cage. It was a 'temporary' cage.
Fishing. Next to the carp. They know who I am.
Holding the noble's goblet. He doesn't drink. He just likes it held.
Pumping. For four days. Nobody told me to stop.

voxpops.q: How do you deal with someone's tantrum?
answers: I ask them about their cat. Calms them right down.
Wine. A bucket of it. Theirs or mine.
Get out of range, then out of the next room's range.
As the captain of the guard, I just write it down.
I start my own. It's a distraction technique.
Hand them a mug to throw that's already chipped.

voxpops.q: If you could buy anything at the depot, what?
answers: Sunlight in a jar. I'd keep it closed though.
Steel. A mountain of it. I'm a weaponsmith with dreams.
Another sock. Matched. Fine. Any color.
Exotic fruit. I'll eat anything that isn't a plump helmet.
A one-way ticket to the mountainhome. Kidding. Mostly.
Those elf boats. I'd sink them. On purpose.

voxpops.q: Which scares you more: magma or water?
answers: Water. Magma at least tells you it's coming.
Magma. Water's just wet magma. Hm. That came out wrong.
Both, but I'm a miner. Fear is the job.
Water. I live under the aquifer. Every drip, I flinch.
Magma. I lost my eyebrows. They aren't growing back.
Neither. The carp are the problem.

voxpops.q: Where should we build the new tavern?
answers: Next to the old tavern. Two taverns. You'd never have to leave.
Closer to the hospital, for efficiency.
Under the library, so the scholars come down sometimes.
Far, far from the well. We've learned.
Inside the militia barracks. Morale has never been higher.
Wherever I am. Just put a keg on me.

help_wanted.text: WANTED: Hauler. Must enjoy carrying one stone very far, then back. Bring your own legs. Apply at the stockpile, which you will also be carrying.
SEEKING: Brewer with steady hands and steadier nerves. Fort is three days from a tantrum. No pressure. Some pressure. All the pressure.
CAT HERDER needed. Experience with twenty cats preferred; experience with two hundred cats required. Compensation: one cat, which will choose you.
WANTED: Bookkeeper. Must count things. Must count them again. Must not cry when the numbers change. Office provided; chair pending.
MILITIA RECRUITS: Free armor, free danger room access, free funeral. Babies welcome, apparently. We keep trying to stop this.
SEEKING: Mason to wall us off from the outside. Urgent. Must not ask what's outside. Must not look outside. Applicants who have seen outside, discount.
WANTED: Engraver for the overseer's office. Theme: the overseer, being excellent. A subtle approach will be discouraged.
FISH CLEANER needed. Fish provided. Dignity not provided. Do not make eye contact with the fish.
SEEKING: Surgeon. Must know which end of the saw to hold. Patients strongly prefer applicants who say 'the handle end.'
WANTED: Bard for the tavern. Poetry about granite strongly discouraged. Poetry about anything else gratefully accepted. Kazoo optional.
PUMP OPERATOR: Stand here. Push. Keep pushing. We will tell you when to stop. We will not tell you when to stop.
WANTED: Someone, anyone, to bury {deadname}. Slab is engraved. Coffin is ready. Ghost is getting impatient.
SEEKING: Gem cutter. Our pile of rough gems is growing, and the broker has started saying 'sparkly' in his sleep.
NOBLE'S ASSISTANT: Fetch things, sigh softly, pretend each mandate is reasonable. Must possess a quiet voice and a sturdy helmet.
WANTED: Kobold-spotter. Sit by the stockpiles. If a goblet moves by itself, shout. Snacks provided, nailed to the table.
CHEESEMAKER urgently sought. We have milk. We do not know why. The goats do not know why either.
SEEKING: Woodcutter to brave the surface and the elves' opinions. Bring an axe, earplugs, and a firm position on trees.
WANTED: Tavern keeper. Must catch mugs. Must also serve mugs. Ideally in that order, and not the reverse.
SCHOLAR wanted for the library. Read, write, argue with self. Previous scholar was lost to a book about rocks and is not coming back.
WANTED: Minecart rider. There are no drivers; you get in and hope. Helmet mandatory. Exit strategy optional.
BUTCHER needed. Animals provided. Strong stomach required. Strong opinions about the word 'tallow' preferred.
WANTED: Dwarf to open the gate when the caravan arrives and close it when goblins arrive. Please do not confuse the two again.
SEEKING: Clothier. Our clothes are mostly holes. The holes are mostly unhappy. Reasonable pay, unreasonable demand.
WANTED: One left sock. Will pay handsomely. No questions asked about where it has been, or who has been wearing it.
SEEKING: Ranger who can tell a goblin from a bush. Our last ranger reported 'many hostile bushes' and has been reassigned.
ARCHITECT: Design a bridge that rises when goblins approach. Must not rise while dwarves are standing on it. Ideally.
WANTED: Glassmaker. Sand provided. Fire provided. Confidence that it won't all melt the wrong way, sadly, not provided.
HOSPITAL ORDERLY: Fetch water. That's it. That's the job. Nobody in fort history has done it. Be the first.
SEEKING: Dwarf willing to look inside the well. Just a quick peek. It's probably nothing. Please ignore the singing.
CARAVAN GREETER for {fort}: Smile, wave, steal nothing. Two out of three is acceptable.
WANTED: Farmer to grow plump helmets, sweet pods, and morale. Underground position. Sun not included, and frankly not missed.
DANGER ROOM TESTER: Walk in. Walk out. Report back. Excellent pay, paid to next of kin in advance as a courtesy.

real_estate.head: Cozy 1x1 Bedroom, Near Dining
real_estate.text: Freshly dug. Room for one bed or one dwarf standing confidently. Walls smoothed on request. Neighbors: the tavern, loudly.

real_estate.head: Charming Hallway, Lived-In
real_estate.text: Currently home to seven migrants and a goat. Lots of foot traffic, plenty of company, no privacy. The perfect starter home.

real_estate.head: Riverside Hut (Surface)
real_estate.text: Fresh air, sky views, and very attentive fish. Sold as is. Previous owner left in a hurry and now lives in the deepest bedroom.

real_estate.head: Luxury Noble Suite
real_estate.text: Engraved walls, gold furniture, a door that locks. Previous occupant, a baron, was demoted and now sleeps in a closet. Price negotiable by mandate.

real_estate.head: Magma-View Studio
real_estate.text: Unbeatable warmth. Watch the forges glow all night. Occasional smell of singed beard. Fireproof furniture strongly recommended.

real_estate.head: Former Danger Room, Renovated
real_estate.text: Spears removed. Mostly. Spacious, airy, full of character. Helmet recommended in the northeast corner. Do not touch the lever.

real_estate.head: Quiet Tomb, Move-In Ready
real_estate.text: Slab included. Silent neighbors. Ideal for the dwarf who has finished everything. Viewings by appointment; ghosts by surprise.

real_estate.head: Above-Aquifer Penthouse
real_estate.text: Just one floor above the aquifer. Floors damp only in spring. A water feature is included whether you want one or not.

real_estate.head: Burrow With Character
real_estate.text: A former kobold den, lightly cleaned. Comes with several goblets of uncertain origin. Seller asks no questions. Buyer should ask none either.

real_estate.head: Spacious Cavern Lot
real_estate.text: Two hundred tiles of fungus forest. Huge mushrooms. Unclear neighbors. Possible forgotten beast in the back yard; the agent declined to check.

real_estate.head: Cat-Friendly Apartment
real_estate.text: Already contains cats. Will continue containing cats. Cat count rises monthly. Strictly no vacancy for mice.

real_estate.head: Tavern Back Room
real_estate.text: Steps from the bar. Floor sticky, spirit unbroken. Bards practice nightly at no extra charge, unfortunately.

real_estate.head: The Overseer's Old Office
real_estate.text: Recently vacated. Includes desk, chair, and an enormous list of cancelled jobs. Faint sound of someone saying 'wait, pause' still echoes.

real_estate.head: Fixer-Upper Near the Well
real_estate.text: Damp, dark, and full of potential. Previous tenant fell into the well, unrelated to the property. Probably.

real_estate.head: Hospital Bed With a View
real_estate.text: Traction bench and a ceiling of your choice, provided you choose stone. Dedicated staff who will not bring you water.

real_estate.head: Minecart Station Loft
real_estate.text: Fast commute, guaranteed. Occasional minecart through the living room. Sound-dampening walls installed after the third incident.

real_estate.head: The {stone} Manor
real_estate.text: Built entirely of {stone}, which the agent will mention seventeen times during your viewing. Grand. Solid. Very, very {stone}.

real_estate.head: Pump Stack Tower Room
real_estate.text: Rhythmic creaking lulls you to sleep; constant splashing wakes you up. Heated by friction. Lovely view of the dwarf pumping all night.

real_estate.head: Militia Barracks Bunk
real_estate.text: Sleep among the bravest. Snoring in formation. Weapon rack within arm's reach, which is great until someone dreams about goblins.

real_estate.head: Library Nook
real_estate.text: Silent, scholarly, surrounded by books. Ideal for reading, writing, or hiding from nobles, who do not read.

real_estate.head: Trade Depot Kiosk
real_estate.text: Prime commercial location, seasonally busy. Elves stand here and refuse every carving. Strong foot traffic, weak profit.

real_estate.head: Open-Plan Stockpile Corner
real_estate.text: Lovely open corner, formerly the rock stockpile. Still technically the rock stockpile. There are rocks. You will live with the rocks.

real_estate.head: Snowed-In Surface Shack
real_estate.text: Insulated by six feet of snow. Charming wooden walls an elf would weep over. No exit until spring. Ideal for introverts.

real_estate.head: Dining Hall Corner Table
real_estate.text: Officially furniture, practically housing. Long-term residents tolerated if you keep eating. Breakfast, lunch, and dinner within reach.

real_estate.head: Bedroom Above the Moat
real_estate.text: Elevated room with a hatch straight down to the moat. Excellent goblin deterrent. Terrible place to sleepwalk.

real_estate.head: Forge-Side Bunk
real_estate.text: Wake to hammer blows, fall asleep to hammer blows. Warm all year. Includes a glowing anvil and temporary deafness.

announcements.text: A healthy baby girl was born this week. Her first word was 'Urist,' which is a name, a title, and somehow an insult. The family is delighted. The neighbors are confused.
Twins arrived at dawn. One is already trying to haul a stone. The other has bitten the clothier. The family thanks everyone for the socks, only one of which matches.
The fort's cats announce eleven new kittens, bringing the total to 'more.' Adopters may sign up at the tavern. Adopters may also be chosen by kittens without consent.
A baby arrived during the goblin siege and has been carried into battle twice before lunch. Grandparents describe themselves as 'proud, and absolutely terrified.'
A litter of puppies was born under the dining table. The fort's dogs formed a welcoming committee, whose first act was eating somebody's roast.
{citizen} and {citizen2} were wed in the dining hall before friends, family, and three cats. The couple received a masterwork mug, which has already been thrown.
Two miners married this week at the bottom of a freshly dug shaft. The reception was held there too. Guests are asked to stop calling down to ask if it's over.
A mason and a brewer married in a quiet ceremony. The mason built the altar; the brewer stocked the toast. Their love is solid, and also roughly forty proof.
The tavern keeper has married the tavern's best customer, ending a decade of unpaid tabs by converting them into family debt. The couple will honeymoon at the bar.
Two scholars were married in the library by candlelight, very quietly. The vows were written as footnotes. The reception featured snacks and a lively debate about rocks.
Congratulations to {promoted}, newly appointed {post}. Friends say the role has already brought a bigger bedroom, a heavier conscience, and a sudden interest in mandates.
{promoted} has accepted the post of {post}. Asked for comment, {promoted} said 'I didn't ask for this,' then requested a gold throne. A well-earned honor.
The new captain of the guard has been sworn in. Her first act was appointing a hammerer. Her second was asking what a hammerer does. Her third was turning quite pale.
The fort has a new bookkeeper. Her predecessor was found counting barrels in his sleep and has been gently moved to hauling. Welcome! The ledger is under that boulder.
{masterwright} has been hailed as the fort's finest craftsdwarf after producing {masterwork}. Admirers crowd the workshop. The workshop has asked them to stop touching things.
A wave of migrants reached the gate carrying everything they own, which was one pick and a bucket. Welcome! Bedrooms will be dug as soon as the hall floor is full.
{pop} dwarves now call {fort} home after the latest arrivals. Older residents have welcomed them warmly, mostly by showing them where the good mugs are hidden.
The caravan has arrived bearing goods from distant lands: cheese, bins of cheese, and one merchant who has not stopped talking about cheese since spring.
A lone traveler has arrived claiming to be a poet. The tavern has been advised. The resident bard has been advised more firmly. Readings resume once the rivalry cools.
A stray dog wandered in, decided it lives here, and was named honorary hauler. It has not hauled anything. It has been praised constantly regardless.
A diplomat from the mountainhome has arrived to inspect the fortress. He asked to see the beds. We have asked him to wait in the hall, possibly for some time.
{moodname} has emerged from a strange mood holding {artifact}, a {artifact_item} of startling beauty, then went straight to bed and asked not to be congratulated until spring.
Happy anniversary to the well, which has served faithfully, swallowed three dwarves, and inspired most of our ghost stories. Here's to many more buckets.
Another year has passed since the founding of {fort}. Celebrations will be held in the dining hall. Strike the earth! Then come eat. Then strike the earth again.
The fort's oldest barrel of wine turns five today. It has survived two tantrums, one flood, and a bookkeeper. Nobody is allowed to open it. Nobody remembers why.
Ten years since the Great Catsplosion. Survivors will gather in the tavern for a moment of silence, then a moment of sneezing. Please leave all cats at home, if they let you.
It has been one whole week since miners struck {mineral}. They are still standing around it, admiring it. Production has stopped. Spirits have rarely been higher.
A hunter and a woodcutter announce their engagement. They met while fleeing the same elf. The wedding date depends entirely on whether the elf comes back.
A gem setter proposed with a ring of her own making, a ☼brass ring☼ of real stubbornness. He said yes after the appraisal. Love is beautiful, and also fairly valued.
{citizen_first} is engaged! The lucky dwarf was found in the tavern, which is where most of the fort was found. Gifts may be left at the trade depot, marked 'fragile.'
A militia dwarf and a doctor are engaged. Friends say they met in the hospital, then again in the hospital, then many more times in the hospital. True love heals.
A dwarf proposed to a bard by hiring a second bard to sing the proposal. It was accepted. The second bard is now engaged to a third bard. We are concerned.
